I will keep the full 16.9 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the system I know best, it fits Quzhou County conditions, and I have well irrigation to support stable yields. I am 73, so I will not make the management too complicated or too risky. For wheat, I will use an improved variety instead of old seed, put enough nitrogen for strong tillering, add phosphorus to support roots, and give moderate potassium so the crop stands well. I will irrigate three times if water conditions allow, because wheat here depends heavily on timely water at key stages. I will use rotary tillage for wheat land preparation, because it is easier on labor and faster for me than deep ploughing every year. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed, because maize responds well to that and gives me more stable production. I will fertilize maize a bit more heavily on nitrogen than wheat, keep phosphorus moderate, and use some potassium to support grain filling and lodging resistance. I will irrigate maize twice, mainly around jointing and grain filling if rainfall is not enough. I will keep pesticide use moderate on both crops, only enough to protect yield, because I want steady production without adding unnecessary cost or field work.
